description: Dependency-aware hard gates for the registered and re-entrant fly-FGS and historical NOD1 visual-to-flight simulator paths, including causal online bridge/mechanics handoff, true force-stage intervention semantics, independent-process checkpoint re-entry with source receipts, explicit unresolved effector-lane hypotheses, canonical closed-loop orchestration, exact component checkpoint continuation, and scheduled live-circuit integration plus paired force-stage propagation through native FlyBody/MuJoCo. Empirical cases require held-out public evidence receipts.

cases.title: Canonical contract round trip
cases.claim: Scientific interchange objects survive canonical JSON round trips without semantic or digest drift.

tolerance_source.rationale: An immutable report must have exactly the same canonical digest after a lossless round trip.

cases.title: Causal timestamp discipline
cases.claim: No component consumes a sample before its declared availability timestamp.

tolerance_source.rationale: Future-state access invalidates a closed-loop causal claim and is never tolerated.
Sampled voltages and spike events must cross the public circuit-to-DN boundary no earlier than declared source availability plus the configured bridge delay.

cases.title: Causal image-derived visual golden suite
cases.claim: The analytic retinal and motion front end satisfies registered zero-motion, flicker, direction-mirror, phase-periodicity, onset-continuity, and availability invariants without reading semantic scene velocity.

tolerance_source.rationale: A spatially uniform retinal field has no adjacent-receptor direction signal.
Simultaneous full-field flicker may create temporal transients but cannot define a direction.
Equal and opposite panoramic grating motion must produce antisymmetric detector output.
Zero and two-pi phase are the same analytic stimulus and must not be duplicated as distinct conditions.
The figure centre and texture phase are anchored continuously at delayed onset.
A retinal frame cannot enter the motion detector before exposure and sensor latency complete.

cases.title: Causal retinal-to-body vertical slice
cases.claim: A deterministic analytic retinal sequence traverses the reduced NOD1 surrogate, causal DN/VNC bridge, individual muscles, hinge, and reduced mechanics with finite outputs and preserved source frames.

tolerance_source.rationale: No body pose, velocity, or angular velocity may be NaN or infinite.
Every input retinal frame remains attached to the pipeline run.
The executable path must preserve named individual steering channels rather than only side means.
The vertical slice must execute mechanics rather than stop at a motor trace.

cases.title: Causal retinal-to-FlyBody worker vertical slice
cases.claim: A deterministic preferred-direction retinal sequence traverses the explicitly reduced NOD1 surrogate, causal DN/VNC bridge, named steering muscles, virtual hinge, six-axis actuator adapter, FlyBody aerodynamics, and whole-body MuJoCo state; matched uniform-scene, repeated preferred-direction, named-side MN-silence, and repeated MN-silence runs must begin from identical state and time bases, reproduce deterministically, preserve exact records upstream and outside the declared intervention cut, remove the target event no earlier than its availability boundary, and produce nonzero target-muscle, desired-wing, measured-wing, and body-state deltas.

tolerance_source.rationale: The worker vertical slice must execute the named FlyBody adapter rather than silently falling back to reduced physics.
No FlyBody pose, velocity, fluid force, or fluid torque may be NaN or infinite.
The episode runner must preserve the exact compiled FlyBody root/thorax initial position instead of replacing it with a synthetic origin or center-of-mass assumption.
The worker path must retain named individual muscle state through the adapter boundary.
The worker path must preserve measured six-axis MuJoCo wing qpos/qvel separately from desired virtual-hinge kinematics.
The worker must expose MuJoCo's articulated subtree center of mass separately from root/thorax qpos.

The moving, uniform-scene, repeated moving, named-side MN-silence, and repeated MN-silence conditions must reset to the same root, articulated, and measured-wing initial state; standardized absolute differences may contain only floating-point roundoff.
All visual-ablation, repeat, and named-side MN-intervention runs must expose the same retinal, circuit, and physics sample counts and timestamps; only floating-point roundoff is tolerated.

Repeating either the preferred-direction condition or its typed named-side MN-silence intervention with the same configuration, seed, reset state, and clocks must reproduce neural, muscle, wing, aerodynamic, and body trajectories to floating-point roundoff.
Repeating the typed MN-b3-left silence with identical retinal records, seed, reset state, and clocks must reproduce its complete exploratory pipeline output to floating-point roundoff.
A typed MN intervention is applied after retinal sampling, reduced-circuit execution, and descending-neuron encoding, so those immutable records must remain exactly equal.
Channel-local random streams and a named-side MN cut require every non-target bridge and runtime motor-event inventory to remain exactly unchanged.

Every non-target intrinsic activation, force, and phase-memory trace must retain exactly the same key, shape, dtype, and values. Cumulative work is excluded because changed shared-wing velocity can alter work downstream without changing intrinsic non-target muscle state.

The fixed preferred-direction/seed fixture must contain an actionable MN-b3-left event before its silence can serve as a causal-cut test. This is a manufactured software excitation, not a biological response-rate claim.
The full-episode typed MN-b3-left silence must remove its target bridge event and downstream runtime event without post-hoc trace editing.

The typed full-episode MN-b3-left intervention must set every target inferred-rate sample to zero before seeded event generation; the maximum absolute value detects positive and negative nonzero samples.
Every actionable baseline target event must enter the flight runtime at or after its declared bridge availability timestamp.
Removing the manufactured target event must change the named target muscle activation; the magnitude has no biological authority.
The target-muscle change must reach at least one desired virtual-hinge wing channel; the magnitude has no biological authority.
The typed target cut must propagate through the adapter into a changed measured MuJoCo wing trajectory; the magnitude has no biological authority.
The typed target cut must reach final FlyBody root state under the fixed software fixture; this nonzero result is not a biological effect-size or stable-flight claim.
With identical seed, clocks, and baseline commands, visual ablation may change only circuit-driven steering channels; non-steering muscle activation must remain identical to floating-point roundoff.
The visual-to-muscle worker path must deliver a nonzero generalized wing command to MuJoCo.
The worker path must record a nonzero root-total fluid force rather than substituting reduced-order or zero telemetry.
At least one measured FlyBody wing axis must move; desired virtual-hinge motion alone cannot satisfy the end-to-end worker gate.
The preferred-direction visual condition must realize at least one seeded circuit-driven steering-MN event; baseline power-muscle events cannot satisfy this metric.
The matched uniform-scene run must not manufacture circuit-driven steering events.
At least one named circuit-driven steering muscle must receive and express a generated event.
With identical seed and clocks, removing retinal motion must change at least one circuit-driven steering-muscle activation.
The visual steering event must alter virtual-hinge output relative to the common-seed uniform-scene run.
The visual steering event must propagate across the adapter into a changed measured MuJoCo wing trajectory.
The measured visual steering perturbation must reach FlyBody body state; position, velocity, quaternion, and angular velocity are standardized by 1 mm, 1 m/s, 1, and 100 rad/s before taking the norm.

cases.title: Reduced closed-loop yaw software invariants
cases.claim: The explicitly reduced visual-to-yaw loop obeys declared causal latencies, produces deterministic mirror-symmetric negative feedback, and cannot manufacture control torque from a uniform scene.

tolerance_source.rationale: Every rendered observation and neural/muscle command must respect its declared availability time and zero-order hold.
The manufactured yaw perturbation must end below one quarter of its matched open-loop rate; this is a software-control oracle, not a biological target.
Integrated absolute yaw rate must be lower than 55% of the matched open-loop manufactured case.
Equal and opposite manufactured yaw initial states must remain mirror symmetric to numerical precision.
A spatially uniform rendered scene must not create optic-flow control torque.

cases.title: NOD1 Hines solver manufactured solution
cases.claim: The cable solver agrees with a dense linear solve at the registered voltage and scaled residual tolerances.

tolerance_source.rationale: The dense and tree solves represent the same finite-dimensional linear system.
Scaled error uses the registered rtol=1e-8 and atol=1e-9 V acceptance rule.

cases.title: Reduced analytic timestep convergence
cases.claim: For the deterministic reduced analytic baseline, refining the physics step from 0.1 ms to 0.05 ms changes integrated impulse and standardized 100 ms body state by less than two percent.

tolerance_source.rationale: The reduced test backend uses the same preregistered two-percent impulse drift ceiling as the authoritative target.
Standardized terminal body-state drift must remain below two percent for the reduced test backend.

cases.title: Frozen Chromium Worker and Python NOD1 parity
cases.claim: A source-, deployment-, configuration-, and replay-input-locked Chromium Web Worker trace agrees with the local Python backend on four declared NOD1 cable readouts and summary metrics.

tolerance_source.rationale: The 0.05 mV engineering threshold was preregistered in the immutable Chromium/Python capture fixture; it establishes numerical parity, not biological validity.
The one-percent engineering threshold was preregistered in the immutable Chromium/Python capture fixture; it establishes numerical parity, not biological validity.

cases.title: Pinned analytic FlyBody compatibility regression
cases.claim: The pinned FlyBody adapter reproduces its immutable beat-wrapped analytic compatibility fixture; this is not a released-policy or stable-flight baseline.

tolerance_source.rationale: The normalized error divides each residual by the tolerance in this registered adapter fixture; the fixture has no biological or released-policy authority.

cases.title: Fresh-adapter FlyBody checkpoint re-entry
cases.claim: A hash-protected MuJoCo mjSTATE_INTEGRATION checkpoint taken after five 0.1 ms transitions restores into a separately compiled, receipt-matched FlyBody adapter and reproduces the complete exposed checkpoint state and next six transitions exactly. Corrupt envelopes and a validly rehashed cross-model identity are rejected before adapter state mutation. This is a deterministic worker-runtime claim, not stable flight or biological validation.

tolerance_source.rationale: Every public root, wing, actuator, fluid-wrench, and power value must be bit-identical at the restored boundary.
The separately compiled adapter must reproduce every exposed value for all six continuation transitions exactly.
A content mutation without a matching envelope digest must be rejected.
A validly rehashed checkpoint carrying another compiled-model identity must be rejected independently of envelope integrity.
An incompatible restore attempt must leave every exposed adapter state and telemetry value unchanged.

cases.title: Registered Chromium NOD1-to-FlyBody worker vertical slice
cases.claim: The exact content-addressed 1,208-cell Chromium circuit fixture traverses four registered NOD1 voltage readouts, the causal DN/VNC bridge, named wing MNs and muscles, the virtual hinge, and native FlyBody/MuJoCo for the complete half-open 0.5-second capture; an exact repeat and a typed MN-iv1-right cut must preserve reset/timebase identity, remain local upstream, use no contact-bearing transition through 50 ms, and propagate through physics-rate actuator torque, fluid force, physics-rate measured wing state, and body state. This establishes a non-dead deterministic software path, not biological calibration or stable flight.

tolerance_source.rationale: The worker must consume the registered 100-sample, four-readout output of the frozen 1,208-cell Chromium circuit, with no substituted retinal frames or Python comparator voltages.
Circuit, bridge, motor, physics, diagnostics, and logged endpoint clocks must all preserve the registered 0.5-second half-open source duration.
The final source sample at 0.495 s must reach DN availability at 0.498 s and motor availability at the 0.500 s episode boundary rather than being silently dropped.
The marquee frozen-circuit episode must execute native FlyBody/MuJoCo rather than silently falling back to reduced physics.
Both baseline and intervention must contain only finite body, wing, aerodynamic, and muscle values.
A 0.5-second episode at the mandatory 0.1 ms FlyBody step contains exactly 5,000 native physics steps.
Baseline and typed-cut runs must reset to the same compiled root, articulated COM, and measured six-axis wing state.
The target cut may alter values but not circuit or physics timestamps.
Repeating the exact fixture with the same seed, reset state, model, and clocks must reproduce neural, muscle, actuator, contact, aerodynamic, wing, and body traces to floating-point roundoff.

The native worker must expose exact physics-rate MuJoCo contact-point counts from each pre-integration state used for a transition so unconstrained-airborne and contact-constrained dynamics cannot be conflated.
Both paired episodes must begin airborne with no detected ground-plane contact point after the explicit MuJoCo forward pass.

No 0.1 ms transition ending at or before 50 ms may use a pre-integration state with a detected ground-plane contact point, so ground-contact constraints cannot influence the registered airborne causal comparison.
The registered circuit output must produce at least one circuit-derived steering-MN event; baseline flight-state inputs cannot satisfy this metric.
At least one named steering muscle must express circuit-derived activation.
Muscle and hinge output must deliver a nonzero generalized wing torque to native MuJoCo.
The native worker must expose a nonzero root-total FlyBody fluid force.
At least one measured MuJoCo wing axis must move; desired virtual-hinge kinematics alone cannot pass.
A typed MN cut occurs downstream of the fixture and DN encoding, so those exact source records must remain unchanged.
Channel-local random streams require all non-target bridge and runtime event inventories to remain exactly unchanged.
All non-target intrinsic activation, force, and phase-memory traces must remain exactly unchanged.
The fixed fixture and seed must contain an actionable MN-iv1-right event before its causal cut can be evaluated.
The preregistered MN-iv1-right target must have an available generated event within the contact-free 0–50 ms causal-isolation window.
Full-episode MN-iv1-right silence must remove both bridge and runtime target events without trace editing.
The typed intervention must set every target inferred-rate sample to zero before seeded event generation.
Every actionable target event must enter the runtime no earlier than its declared bridge availability.
Removing the target event must change its named muscle activation during the contact-free 0–50 ms window; the magnitude has no biological authority.
The target-muscle change must reach the desired virtual-hinge wing state during the contact-free 0–50 ms window.

The typed cut must propagate through the actuator adapter into a changed physics-rate measured MuJoCo wing trajectory during the contact-free 0–50 ms window; logging-rate point samples cannot satisfy this metric.
The typed cut must change the physics-rate external MuJoCo wing-actuator torque during the contact-free 0–50 ms window; logging-rate point samples cannot satisfy this metric.
The changed measured wing state must alter the physics-rate root-total FlyBody fluid force during the contact-free 0–50 ms window; logging-rate point samples cannot satisfy this metric.
The target cut must reach FlyBody root state by 50 ms before any ground contact; this is not a biological effect-size claim.

cases.title: FlyBody open-loop adapter convergence stress test
cases.claim: With the same prescribed 0.2 ms zero-order-held wing-torque program, FlyBody refinements from 0.1 to 0.05 to 0.025 ms remain below two-percent impulse and standardized body-state drift, converge monotonically, stay airborne, and exercise wings and fluid forces.

tolerance_source.rationale: The fixed-command 0.1/0.05 ms aerodynamic-impulse drift must be no more than two percent.
The fixed-command 0.05/0.025 ms aerodynamic-impulse drift must be no more than two percent.
The fixed-command 0.1/0.05 ms standardized terminal body-state drift must be no more than two percent.
The fixed-command 0.05/0.025 ms standardized terminal body-state drift must be no more than two percent.
The finer refinement must not increase either registered convergence error.
The 0.1 m spawn must remain at least 0.05 m above the ground so contact does not contaminate the numerical comparison.
Every refinement must generate nontrivial fluid force so the gate exercises aerodynamics rather than a zero-input trajectory.
Every refinement must move at least one reviewed wing axis through 0.05 rad so a trivially static model cannot pass.

cases.title: Released-policy FlyBody steady-flight and saccade convergence
cases.claim: Using official FlyBody release archives 51196859 (flight-imitation data and measured WPG) and 44815195 (the ordinary trained-flight SavedModel), the reviewed original observation ordering and CanonicalSpecWrapper inference semantics, and pinned runtime dependencies, refining physics from 0.1 ms to 0.05 ms changes integrated impulse and standardized 100 ms body state by less than two percent for both frozen steady-flight and saccade fixtures. No standalone normalization artifact is assumed; learned LayerNorm parameters belong to the SavedModel.

tolerance_source.rationale: The released-policy steady-flight fixture must limit integrated impulse drift to two percent.
The released-policy steady-flight fixture must limit standardized body-state drift to two percent.
The released-policy saccade fixture must limit integrated impulse drift to two percent.
The released-policy saccade fixture must limit standardized body-state drift to two percent.

cases.title: Cross-atlas identifier integrity
cases.claim: The frozen evidence graph contains no direct individual-neuron joins across identifier spaces and declares every crosswalk explicitly.

tolerance_source.rationale: Individual FlyWire and MANC identifiers may never be directly joined.
Cross-specimen transport must be represented by at least one explicit type-level crosswalk.

cases.title: Frozen female BANC/FANC wing-pathway evidence
cases.claim: Content-addressed BANC v888 and FANC v840 snapshots independently preserve structural NOD1→DNp26→wing-MN observations and the published wing premotor matrix without cross-atlas individual-neuron joins or physiological-weight interpretation.

tolerance_source.rationale: Every upstream BANC/FANC table is retained with its exact byte count, SHA-256, release, and source URI.
BANC and FANC individual-neuron identifiers occupy separate identity spaces and may not be joined directly.
Topological premotor candidates remain unresolved until an explicit evidence-scored crosswalk exists.
Four frozen BANC aggregate edges contain 487 structural synapses from NOD1 to contralateral DNp26; this is topology, not physiological strength.
The registered female BANC snapshot contains 62 proofread wing motor neurons, 31 on each dataset side.
Four BANC wing-MN rows (PSn_u and MNxm01 bilaterally) remain explicitly unresolved rather than silently promoted.
Eighteen registered BANC DNp26→wing-MN edges total 129 raw structural synapses, correcting the earlier provisional count of 131.
The published one-sided FANC v840 wing premotor matrix contains 1,784 presynaptic rows.
The thresholded published FANC matrix contains 144,668 raw structural synapses across 7,289 nonzero pairs.
Every recomputed FANC matrix row total must equal its published MN_syn_total value.
The two explicitly annotated FANC DNp26 rows independently total 153 structural synapses onto named wing-MN columns.

Every runtime DNp26 steering-path structural mask and count must exactly match the aggregate named-muscle observations recomputed from the registered BANC fixture; counts remain non-physiological topology metadata.

cases.title: Causal date-held-out steering-muscle wing prediction
cases.claim: On acquisition-date-held-out Melis recordings, a prediction issued at the onset of left wingbeat k uses only the nine completed wingbeats k-9 through k-1 (twelve left steering-muscle fluorescence summaries plus measured wingbeat frequency) to predict the 80 left-wing Legendre coefficients for wingbeat k with phase-domain kinematic error no worse than a matched causal retraining of the pinned Melis CNN. This claim is limited to one-wingbeat-ahead left-wing kinematics and does not validate bilateral flight, muscle force, sclerite mechanics, aerodynamics, or free flight.

required_evidence.description: Exact CC0 CaltechDATA HDF5 receipt with source byte count and MD5 plus independently observed SHA-256.
Immutable HDF5 topology receipt covering every session, acquisition date, movie, N_wbs value, array name, shape, dtype, eligible causal window, and missing or non-finite value.
Immutable session-to-acquisition-date mapping and any available biological-individual or preparation crosswalk; the claim remains date-held-out if animal identity is unavailable.

Pre-fit whole-acquisition-date 23/5/5 calibration/validation/held-out assignment, stable sample IDs, exclusions, and zero-overlap audit for dates, sessions, movies, source wingbeats, and derived windows.
Per-sample feature indices, measurement and availability times, issue time, target onset, and proof that no same-beat, future, centered, or acausally preprocessed value is consumed.
Feature order, train-only transforms, stable-ID exclusion rules, coefficient order and units, and pinned Legendre reconstruction implementation and phase grid.
Pinned causal retraining of the reviewed Melis CNN source with resolved architecture, runtime, seeds, optimizer, validation-only model selection, frozen checkpoint, and frozen held-out predictions.
Candidate model and parameter hashes, adapter to the 80-coefficient target, calibration trial IDs, fit diagnostics, and frozen predictions.
Pinned hierarchical phase-angle and coefficient metrics, date-level bootstrap, matched-sample audit, code/runtime hash, and per-wingbeat/movie/session/date outputs.
Freeze timestamp, no-held-out-access log, evaluator hash, one-time execution ID, and immutable targets, baseline predictions, candidate predictions, and metrics.

tolerance_source.rationale: Every empirical byte must match the reviewed source receipt before a held-out claim is evaluated.
An acquisition date and all of its descendants must belong to exactly one permanent split.
A recording session must never contribute to more than one split.
A movie must never contribute to more than one split.
No source wingbeat or derived nine-beat window may cross a split boundary.
A prediction for wingbeat k may consume only completed wingbeats k-9 through k-1.
Every fluorescence and frequency value must be available by the prediction issue time; ordinal indexing alone is insufficient.
Scalers, imputers, learned filters, and all preprocessing parameters must be fit on the calibration split only.
Held-out targets or predictions must not influence architecture, hyperparameters, checkpointing, exclusions, or stopping.
Candidate and matched baseline must be scored on identical frozen held-out sample IDs and masks.
Every candidate and baseline coefficient prediction must be finite.
The preregistered 33-date 70/15/15 split assigns exactly five independent acquisition-date groups to held-out evaluation.
The one-sided 95% acquisition-date cluster-bootstrap upper bound of hierarchical phase-angle RMSE ratio must establish non-inferiority to the matched causal baseline.
No theta, eta, phi, or xi axis may be worse than the matched causal baseline at the one-sided 95% date-cluster upper bound.
Coefficient-space performance guards against a phase reconstruction that hides systematic representation error.
The matched causal CNN must itself outperform the calibration-only mean predictor at the one-sided 95% date-cluster upper bound before it can be a meaningful baseline.

cases.title: Held-out asynchronous power-muscle physiology
cases.claim: The power-muscle model reproduces held-out firing, calcium, wingbeat-frequency, and splay-state relationships within source-backed uncertainty.

required_evidence.description: Exact CC-BY experimental-archive receipts and a source-recording lineage that collapses every raw, workbook, NPY, AVI/TIFF, and event-derived representation onto its biological animal and recording.
Exact code/environment archive receipt with the CC-BY-NC restriction preserved and no assumption that derived NPY files are independent from their raw recordings.
Complete per-animal raw calcium movies, ROI traces, fit tables, processing code, and reconciled animal count for the reported calcium cohort; representative and aggregate traces are insufficient.
Immutable animal/recording-grouped calibration, validation, and held-out manifest with cross-sex transfer declared and sealed promotion execution.

tolerance_source.rationale: Every raw and derived empirical artifact must match its reviewed intake-manifest receipt before scoring.
All recordings and representations from one biological individual must remain in one permanent split.
A raw recording and every event, workbook, NPY, image, and movie derived from it must belong to exactly one split.
Multiple representations of the same source recording may not be counted as independent trials.
Model and preprocessing fits may reference calibration individuals only.
Held-out responses may not influence exclusions, endpoint selection, parameters, checkpoints, or stopping.
Male physiology used for the canonical female simulator must be explicitly represented and scored as cross-sex transfer evidence.
Every held-out prediction and source observation admitted to a metric must be finite.
The one-sided 95% biological-individual-cluster upper bound of indirect-MN firing-rate error divided by its registered source uncertainty must not exceed one.

The one-sided 95% biological-individual-cluster upper bound of calcium-trace error divided by registered measurement uncertainty must not exceed one; incomplete aggregate-only calcium evidence cannot supply this metric.
The one-sided 95% biological-individual-cluster upper bound of wingbeat-frequency error divided by registered source uncertainty must not exceed one.

The one-sided 95% biological-individual-cluster upper bound of the registered splay-state effect error divided by source uncertainty must not exceed one; this narrow challenge is not treated as general force validation.

cases.title: Leakage-safe DNg02 positive-control flight response
cases.claim: On a permanent five-driver-line sealed-test partition of female tethered-flight trials, the frozen simulator must predict the Methods-aligned half-second wingbeat-amplitude response to DNg02 optogenetic activation, including a positive activation effect and positive population dependence across targeted-pair-count levels. Open-loop striped-drum and closed-loop stripe endpoints are scored separately with equal driver-line weight and no held-out access before predictions are frozen; targeted pairs remain a driver-line proxy, not an exact per-animal recruited-cell count or free-flight physiological gain.

required_evidence.description: Content-addressed expected identities for the two sealed CC-BY HDF5 outcomes, three source-analysis scripts, and canonical README; this metadata-only receipt contains no HDF5 outcomes and does not itself unblock promotion.

Immutable 7/3/5 SHA-ranked driver-line split, stable source-coordinate identities, Methods-aligned half-second endpoint, equal-line inference, 10000-draw deterministic bootstrap, exclusions, coverage, and frozen-prediction contract.

Peer-reviewed DNg02 activation evidence and protocol context; the registered Methods endpoint and leakage controls are governed by the frozen local v3 protocol rather than reconstructed figure coordinates.

Reviewed content-addressed mapping from each source timestamp to optogenetic activation onset, fixed from source metadata without reading or optimizing against wingbeat-amplitude outcomes; this required receipt is not yet sealed.
One-shot trusted-splitter execution under the common sealed-held-out protocol after model, evaluator, environment, exclusions, and all ten protocol-by-line predictions are frozen.

tolerance_source.rationale: Every HDF5, code, README, and derived manifest must match the reviewed source receipt before scoring.
No sealed-test value, missingness mask, aggregate, exclusion count, or plot may be disclosed before evaluator and predictions are frozen.
All 15 driver lines must retain their preregistered SHA-ranked 7/3/5 assignment in every protocol and derived representation.
A driver line and every fly and activation trial assigned to it must occur in exactly one permanent partition.
Open-loop striped-drum and closed-loop stripe observations and metrics must never be pooled.
Every immutable line, dataset-local fly, activation-trial, and time-sample identity must resolve to exactly one source coordinate without case-folding or cross-protocol biological-subject inference.
Baseline, response, delta, filtered, summary, and bootstrap derivatives must retain their source identity and may never be counted as independent flies, trials, or lines.
Held-out lines may not influence exclusions, response windows, parameters, checkpoints, or stopping.
No fly, trial, line, time interval, or protocol may be excluded from effect size, sign, variance, residual, influence, appearance, or simulator agreement.
One finite prediction must be frozen for each of five sealed-test driver lines in each protocol before any held-out outcome is released.
Every admitted source endpoint, frozen prediction, null denominator, bootstrap draw, and reported metric must be finite; a non-finite value blocks rather than being coerced.
Every source timestamp must use the reviewed activation-onset metadata mapping; onset may not be inferred or shifted using wingbeat-amplitude outcomes.
Every admitted fly must retain exactly 30 acquisition-ordered activation trials; trials may not be ranked, replaced, or selected by response.
The open-loop endpoint is scored only if all five permanently assigned sealed-test driver lines are evaluable with at least three admitted flies per line.
The closed-loop endpoint is scored only if all five permanently assigned sealed-test driver lines are evaluable with at least three admitted flies per line.
The open-loop sealed-test lines must span at least two distinct frozen targeted-pair proxy levels without reassignment or substitution.
The closed-loop sealed-test lines must span at least two distinct frozen targeted-pair proxy levels without reassignment or substitution.
The one-sided 95% driver-line-cluster lower bound for the open-loop optogenetic wingbeat-amplitude effect must be positive after conversion from degrees to radians.
The one-sided 95% driver-line-cluster lower bound for the closed-loop optogenetic wingbeat-amplitude effect must be positive after conversion from degrees to radians.
The one-sided 95% driver-line-cluster lower bound of the open-loop population-dependence slope must be positive; targeted pair count remains a driver-line proxy.
The one-sided 95% driver-line-cluster lower bound of the closed-loop population-dependence slope must be positive; targeted pair count remains a driver-line proxy.
The one-sided 95% driver-line-cluster upper bound of open-loop curve RMSE divided by a calibration-only line-mean null must not exceed one.
The one-sided 95% driver-line-cluster upper bound of closed-loop curve RMSE divided by a calibration-only line-mean null must not exceed one.

cases.title: Registered fly-FGS fixed-step circuit integrity
cases.claim: The exact content-addressed upstream fly-FGS engine, circuit bundle, source manifest, and non-dead fixed-step capture retain their registered inventory, 48-step pre-roll, half-open 100-sample timebase, four-NOD1 trace digest, full-state projections, and downstream exclusion boundary. This frozen-regression gate does not establish a second execution, Chromium parity, physiology, motor validity, or behavior.

tolerance_source.rationale: The registered capture, manifest, four source assets, executable-input allowlist, cell/event/cable inventory, type counts, T5 absence, and four NOD1 roots must remain exactly content-addressed.
The capture must retain its exact 48-step static pre-roll and 100 samples on the 5 ms half-open [0, 0.5 s) fixed-step grid.
Strict adaptation of the four registered NOD1 voltage channels must reproduce the preregistered CircuitOutputTrace digest; this is a serialization regression, not independent runtime determinism.
Every motor-bound NOD1 voltage must be an exact projection of the registered 1,684-cell matrix, and each raw application-side pooled NOD1 trace must equal its two-cell mean.
The canonical moving-figure sweep must produce a nonzero pooled T4 activity excursion so a flat/dead visual capture cannot pass.
At least one registered motor-bound NOD1 channel must have nonzero SI-voltage excursion so a dead downstream circuit cannot pass.
No rejected fly-FGS DN gain, motor, muscle, prescribed-wing, yaw, or toy-body field may occur as a data-bearing capture key.

cases.title: Incremental fly-FGS runtime parity
cases.claim: A fresh process running only the content-addressed fly-FGS circuit engine and bundle with SI scene/body controls reproduces every registered value across the complete 100-sample capture: the 1,684-cell voltage and activity state, 1,441-point T4a normalized-luminance input, pooled display traces, and four motor-bound NOD1 voltages. This establishes deterministic incremental software equivalence, not calibrated retina, anatomy, physiology, motor output, or behavior.

tolerance_source.rationale: The content-addressed capture binds the source manifest receipt; the runtime must retain its registered snapshot, 5 ms clock, 48-step pre-roll, 100-sample interval, two-asset executable allowlist, and four-channel motor cut.
Every incremental measurement and availability timestamp must exactly equal the registered integer 5 ms grid.
All four individual motor-bound NOD1 voltage channels must be bit-exact across all 100 samples.
Every one of the 168,400 full-cell voltage values must be exactly reproduced; this display state remains motor-ineligible.
Every one of the 168,400 full-cell activity values must be exactly reproduced.
All 144,100 analytic endpoint luminance values at the exact retinotopic T4a coordinates must be reproduced; this is normalized luminance, not irradiance.
Every registered raw-application-side pooled circuit trace must exactly match the incremental readout; application L/R is not anatomical laterality.

cases.title: Fresh-process fly-FGS checkpoint re-entry
cases.claim: A hash-protected checkpoint taken at the aligned 250 ms circuit boundary restores the complete mutable fly-FGS state in a fresh process, rejects tampering before state mutation, reproduces the checkpoint sample exactly, and reaches the same registered final sample and hidden-state digest. This gate covers only the circuit runtime; downstream bridge, muscle, RNG, and MuJoCo checkpoint state remain separate prerequisites for an end-to-end resumable loop.

tolerance_source.rationale: The first registered checkpoint is fixed at sample 50, exactly 250 ms on the 5 ms circuit grid.
A sample-index mutation without a matching payload digest must be rejected before restoration.
Restored full voltage, activity, and T4a input at sample 50 must equal the uninterrupted process exactly.
The fresh-process final full voltage, activity, and T4a input must equal the uninterrupted process exactly.
The complete hidden dynamic-state digest after resumed execution must equal uninterrupted execution.
The restored checkpoint sample must also match every corresponding registered source value and timestamp.
The resumed final sample must also match every corresponding registered source value and timestamp.
